LESSON: SPEED READING

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: GERMAN
Strand: Reading 2.1 Extensive Reading (2 Lessons) By the end of the sub- strand, the lea
Topic 2.2: Speed Reading

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Speed Reading. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What can you do to improve your reading fluency?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify main information from given texts for comprehension
2. appreciate the role of proper pronunciation and intonation for fluency

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: SPEED READING
Subject: GERMAN · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Speed Reading helps you succeed in GERMAN. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: SPEED READING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify main information from given texts for comprehension

What this means
In this part you learn to identify main information from given texts for comprehension. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify main information from given texts for comprehension.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Speed Reading”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify main information from given texts for comprehension. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Appreciate the role of proper pronunciation and intonation for fluency

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the role of proper pronunciation and intonation for fluency. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the role of proper pronunciation and intonation for fluency.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Speed Reading to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the role of proper pronunciation and intonation for fluency. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Speed Reading is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Speed Reading”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify main information from given texts for comprehension)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Speed Reading to a partner. (skill: appreciate the role of proper pronunciation and intonation for fluency)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Speed Reading to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify main information from given texts for comprehension.
3. Practise this skill: appreciate the role of proper pronunciation and intonation for fluency.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Speed Reading from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Speed Reading: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Speed Reading?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What can you do to improve your reading fluency?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Speed Reading means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify main information from given texts for comprehension.
5. Be able to: appreciate the role of proper pronunciation and intonation for fluency.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
